genxml.title: O2 GBE display back end register words
genxml.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
genxml.doc: GBE display back end register words, tables and offsets.

struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: CMAP_FIFO
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: CRS_CTL
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX text port writes 1 after the glyph and colours are loaded; what the other bits mean there is unknown.

struct.name: CRS_POS
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Cursor position, CRS_0. The table gives 16-bit X in bits 15:0 and Y in bits 31:16, reset zero. The spec's functional text (pp. 20-22) calls positions 12-bit, and NetBSD treats the fields as signed. Width and signedness are unresolved. The shipped IRIX text port writes 0 at set-up.

struct.name: CRS_START_XY
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX kernel writes the same vertical part as DID_START_XY, with one line added (0x1000), and the horizontal blank end minus 54 with total pixels added when that is negative; the 54 is a kernel constant. The placement of the parts follows the fields here (inferred).

struct.name: CTRLSTAT
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Pin pair n is data at bit 6+2n and an active-low output enable at bit 7+2n, for n = 0 to 9. Reset is 11 for every pair (data high, output disabled), so every pin is an input. Bit 4 is the monitor sense pin, an external read-only input whose polarity and wiring are not established. Bits 26 (half-phase) and 27 (composite sync polarity) reset to zero. Bits 3:0 are the chip revision, read-only.

struct.name: DID_CONTROL
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX stop routine tests the enable bit at entry, clears it and leaves the word otherwise unwritten; the kernel never writes the table address field.

struct.name: DID_FRAME
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX X module packs a frame entry as block << 19 | offset << 11 | yend, one per horizontal band of lines.

struct.name: DID_INHWCTRL
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: DID_LINE
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX X module packs a line-table entry as index << 11 | xend, one per rectangle in a band and sorted by its last column, in 16-bit units inside a block.

struct.name: DID_START_XY
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX kernel writes a vertical part of minus (vertical blank start minus vertical blank end minus 1) when that difference is positive, else the difference, masked to 12 bits, and a horizontal part of the horizontal blank end minus 20 (total pixels added when the blank end is below 20). The bit placement of the two parts is not stated by the kernel and follows the fields here.

struct.name: DOTCLOCK
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Bits 22 (out of range) and 23 (out of lock) are status bits. The table leaves their reset contents unspecified, and the spec gives no PLL lock time or frequency limits. Bits 25:24 are the PLL test inputs tdwni and tupi, described only as their normal operation state, with reset zero ([gbe-spec] p. 36). The shipped IRIX kernel clears the run bit, writes the timing words, then writes this word with the run bit set and waits 11 milliseconds (DOTCLK_SETTLE_MS). It stores M minus one, N minus one and P unchanged. What the run bit does in the hardware is inferred; the specification leaves it undefined.

struct.name: FP_DE
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX timing routine writes it only for the default set-up and panel set-ups 130 and 131, and only when no dual-channel option is fitted.

struct.name: FP_HDRV
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The three flat-panel drive registers and the three start-preset registers share one layout: two 12-bit counts, "off" or "x" in the low half. The specification names them VT_10 to VT_12 and VT_17 to VT_19 (pages 39 and 40). It compares FP_HDRV, FP_DE and the "x" halves with the horizontal counter and FP_VDRV and the "y" halves with the vertical counter, but it compares both halves of FP_DE with the horizontal counter. The totals shipped software writes for two fixed panels (806 and 771, 1065 and 1024) look like line counts, not pixel counts (inferred from magnitude); which counter FP_DE really uses is unknown. The value the shipped IRIX timing routine writes depends on the board's panel set-up byte and on whether a dual-channel option is fitted.

struct.name: FP_VDRV
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The value the shipped IRIX timing routine writes depends on the board's panel set-up byte and on whether a dual-channel option is fitted.

struct.name: FRM_CONTROL
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX stop routine saves it, clears its enable bit, and later writes it back with its pointer field bumped by one unit.

struct.name: FRM_INHWCTRL
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX start-up sequence polls bit 0 until it equals bit 0 of the value it has just written to the frame control word.

struct.name: FRM_SIZE_PIXEL
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Frame height in pixels, shared by the normal and overlay planes. Reset zero.

struct.name: FRM_SIZE_TILE
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: I2C
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Monitor DDC bus. Bit 0 is the data line and bit 1 the clock line; both reset to 1. The spec gives separate output and synchronized input pins (page 22): a write sets the outputs, and a read returns the bus state, which can differ from the output latch. NetBSD XORs both written and read bits with 3 and calls the fields low active. That is a software expectation (inferred), and the register table alone does not say whether writing 1 releases a line. Whether the reset value 1 means released is therefore not established.

struct.name: I2CFP
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Flat-panel DDC bus, same layout as I2C: data at bit 0 and clock at bit 1, both reset to 1. The spec places external pullups on the flat-panel clock and data outputs (page 4). The inverted-convention caveat under I2C applies here too.

struct.name: MODE_ENTRY
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX kernel rejects window indices of 32 or more and writes entry 0 with 3 at text-port set-up. Its compare mask (0x7fc) leaves the auxiliary field out, and it clears the gamma disable bit before a write when the alternative gamma table is in use. Buffer code: 3 buffers both, 0 marks the window to be skipped by the buffer flip, 1 and 2 exchange on a swap. Pixel type: 0 indexed 8-bit, 1 indexed 12-bit, 2 RG3B2, 4 RGB5, 5 RGB8. The colour-map group's first entry is the group value times 256.

struct.name: OVR_CONTROL
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX stop routine clears its enable bit and leaves the word otherwise unwritten; reading the enable as a DMA enable is inferred.

struct.name: OVR_INHWCTRL
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX start-up sequence polls bit 0 until it equals bit 0 of the value it has just written to the overlay control word.

struct.name: OVR_WIDTH_TILE
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Overlay width must be a multiple of 32 pixels, so the 32-byte remainder is whole pixels at 8 bits (GBE 1.1 pp. 13-14).

struct.name: SYSCLK
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: System PLL test controls, gains and divider ([gbe-spec] p. 37). Bits 1:0 are tdwni and tupi and bits 3:2 tm(1) and tm(0), described as normal operation states; the field below spans all four. Reset has bit 3 set and every other defined bit zero.

struct.name: TILE_LIST_ENTRY
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: VC_0
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: VC_1
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: VC_2
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX video driver clears VC_0 to VC_3 (written as zero when a capture path stops); bit 0 of VC_2 enabling DMA is inferred from its start routine.

struct.name: VC_3
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX video driver clears it when a capture path stops and holds a path byte in it; that reading is inferred from the start routine.

struct.name: VC_START_XY
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX kernel writes the same vertical part as DID_START_XY without the extra line, and the horizontal blank end minus 4. The placement of the parts follows the fields here (inferred).

struct.name: VC_TILES
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: VT_F2RF_LOCK
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Field-to-frame lock line, VT_7. The register table ([gbe-spec] p. 39) puts vt_f2rf, the line where the left/right synchronisation signal toggles, in bits 11:0 and vt_frmlock, the line vt_y is preset to on a frame-lock edge, in bits 23:12, and gives both a reset of zero. The shipped IRIX timing routine stores the vertical blank start line in the high field, and repeats it in the low field when the frame-lock flag bits (mask 0x12) of its timing record are set, else 0xfff.

struct.name: VT_FLAGS
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Output polarity and control bits 6:0 (VT_6). The register table ([gbe-spec] p. 39) names every bit and gives all of them a reset of zero: vsync invert, vsync forced low, hsync invert, hsync forced low, composite sync forced high (4) or low (5), and left/right signal forced high (6). The shipped IRIX timing routine reads it, clears bits 1 and 7, and ORs in 0 or 2 for the board's panel set-up byte 132. What bit 1 does to the hardware is unknown. The value is undefined when the option lookup that feeds it fails.

struct.name: VT_HBLANK
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Horizontal blanking turns off and on at these pixel counts (VT_5). The shipped IRIX timing routine stores it in the interlace case and when no dual-channel option is fitted, packing the active width in the high field and 0xfff in the low field.

struct.name: VT_HCMAP
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX kernel writes the horizontal blank window: start in the high field, end in the low field, in pixels.

struct.name: VT_HPIXEN
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Horizontal pixel-enable window, VT_13. The spec prose says the horizontal and vertical enables combine with OR. The table does not settle that rule. The shipped IRIX kernel parks 0xffffff here before the frame buffer is set up and writes it last in the start-up sequence: the high field is the horizontal blank end minus 0x13 (total pixels added first when that is negative), the low field is (active width + that value - 2) modulo total pixels.

struct.name: VT_HSYNC
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Horizontal sync turns off and on at these pixel counts (VT_3).

struct.name: VT_INTR01
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: VT_INTR23
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings

struct.name: VT_VBLANK
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Vertical blanking turns off and on at these lines (VT_4). The shipped IRIX timing routine stores it in the interlace case and when no dual-channel option is fitted, packing the active height in the high field and 0xfff in the low field.

struct.name: VT_VCMAP
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX kernel writes the vertical blank window: start in the high field, end in the low field, in lines.

struct.name: VT_VPIXEN
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Vertical pixel-enable window, VT_14. The shipped IRIX kernel parks 0xffffff here and writes it last in the start-up sequence with the vertical blank end in the high field and the vertical blank start in the low field.

struct.name: VT_VSYNC
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: Vertical sync turns off and on at these lines (VT_2). The page 38 text for the on row repeats the off comparator, so the positions are established but that description is not.

struct.name: VT_XY
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX start-up sequence compares its whole unmasked value with the vertical blank start line; the stop sequence reads bit 31 as the freeze state and freezes the word by writing VT_XY_FREEZE. The kernel reading derived this offset from the numbering of the other timing words and graded it inferred; the specification's table gives it.

struct.name: VT_XYMAX
struct.from: published GBE 1.1 specification, public Linux and NetBSD O2 framebuffer drivers, and shipped IRIX software readings
struct.doc: The shipped IRIX timing routine writes 0 here, and the start-up sequence writes the totals once the frame buffer is set up. The kernel stores the record's total pixels and total lines, not one less than them; whether the hardware expects one less is unknown.
